facts.t: Roughly five crore names were removed across more than fifteen states
facts.d: The Supreme Court upheld the exercise's constitutionality in ADR v. ECI (2026) — but the verdict came six months after the Bihar polls, so judicial correction could not restore anyone wrongly excluded before that election.

facts.t: Only about a quarter of births were registered in 2007
facts.d: That is the birth year of those turning eighteen by 2025. Requiring birth certificates from such voters imposes a documentary burden that the state's own record-keeping made impossible to meet.

facts.t: Canada's voters never re-prove their eligibility
facts.d: Its National Register of Electors updates continuously through tax, immigration and vital statistics linkages. Germany achieves the same through mandatory municipal residence registration. Mature democracies integrate data rather than sending officials door to door.

bank.q: Which case established that a person already on the electoral roll is presumed a citizen?
o: Lal Babu Hussein v. Electoral Registration Officer (1995)
bank.e: Lal Babu Hussein (1995). SIR was criticised for reversing that presumption by requiring voters absent from the 2002-03 legacy rolls to prove citizenship.

bank.q: With reference to criticisms of SIR, consider the following statements:
s: It reversed the burden of proof on citizenship.
Aadhaar was initially excluded from admissible documents.
It was conducted with generous timelines well removed from election dates.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Compressed timelines close to elections were among the central objections.

bank.q: Which one of the following groups is NOT identified as disproportionately burdened by the documentation requirement?
bank.e: Those with stable documentary histories were least affected. The burden fell on the poor, the illiterate, minorities and the mobile.

bank.as: SIR was criticised as a backdoor National Register of Citizens.
bank.rs: It shifted the burden of proving citizenship onto individuals, encroaching on the Home Ministry's constitutional domain.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — hence the proposal that SIR be confined to roll eligibility, with citizenship questions routed through the Citizenship Act.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the Assam precedent:
s: A past SIR there led to persons being labelled doubtful voters before Foreigners' Tribunals.
Tribunal member qualifications were progressively weakened over time.
Members must still be retired judges, as required since 1964.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The requirement fell from retired judges in 1964 to any lawyer with seven years' experience today.

bank.q: Match List I (country) with List II (roll maintenance model):
pairs: 1. National Register of Electors updated via tax and immigration data
2. Near-automatic registration through mandatory residence registration
3. Rolling annual canvass with Individual Electoral Registration
bank.e: Britain's rolling canvass with data matching, Canada's continuous register, Germany's Meldewesen, and India's periodic intensive revision.

bank.q: Which international standard requires a fair hearing before removal from an electoral roll?
o: UN Human Rights Committee General Comment 25
The Venice Commission Code of Good Practice
bank.e: General Comment 25 — any restriction on the right to vote must rest on objective, reasonable criteria with adequate safeguards.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed reforms EXCEPT:
o: Statutory cooling-off periods before scheduled polls
Accepting Aadhaar and widely held IDs from the outset
Extending the Foreigners' Tribunal model nationwide for appeals
Real-time searchable databases of reasoned deletions
bank.e: That model is expressly criticised — the proposal is for judicially trained tribunals distinct from it.

bank.q: With reference to the ECI's institutional position during SIR, consider the following:
s: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice on the selection committee with a Union Cabinet Minister.
That change is under challenge in Jaya Thakur v. UoI.
The Supreme Court struck down SIR as unconstitutional.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. ADR v. ECI upheld SIR's constitutionality while issuing rights-protective interim directions.

bank.q: What is described as the central tension SIR must resolve?
bank.e: Electoral integrity demands clean rolls; constitutional democracy demands inclusive ones. A democracy is weakened as much by a fraudulent vote as by a silenced genuine one.

bank.as: Post-facto judicial review proved inadequate in the SIR litigation.
bank.rs: The verdict arrived six months after the Bihar polls, by which time wrongful exclusions could not be undone.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — hence the proposal for expedited mechanisms resolving constitutional questions before an election rather than after.
